Files are fetched through a mutable branch, so this is not an exact content-snapshot guarantee or a success flag. Imports without a complete retained observation, including ordinary uploads and historical jobs, have null git_source. Processing, partial and failed imports can retain an observation; inspect status and entries. A retry can replace the observation after another head read, or retain a previous observation if it fails earlier. Separate jobs retain independent observations. JobType.description:
What a job does:
  - ADD_LANGUAGES: an import that adds languages to a branch
  - BACKUP: a stored snapshot of a branch
  - BACKUP_RESTORE: restore selected languages from a snapshot
  - EXPORT: an export of files
  - IMPORT: an import of files
  - WEBHOOK_DELIVERY: a webhook test or redelivery

key.description: Explicit nonblank editable key, including for optional-key formats. Multiple-group formats use dot-separated components with double quotes around literal dots or empty components; inside quotes, escape quotes and backslashes with a backslash. Simple formats use the entire string literally. At most 128 nested key components are accepted. Changed keys must fit the existing rename-history limit of 49,999 Unicode code points after normalization, including internal group separators. An unchanged stored key can be round-tripped without writing history, including a 50,000-code-point key; changing such an existing key returns 409. The larger input bound accommodates quoted escaping. The reserved internal separator <lh> is not accepted.

Resource.description: A resource file or folder (container) within a project branch, exposing its format/path/key metadata and per-language status counts.

content_version.description:
Version of this resource's exported content. A file's number moves whenever any of its languages moves and when a language is
added to or removed from it; a folder's number combines the numbers of the files below it and moves whenever any of them does. It increases whenever anything changes that could alter an export of the file (its segments, their texts and
statuses, keys, order, the file itself, the languages, the export settings, the branch). Compare it with the content_version of
your last export entry for the same file, language and export settings, and export again only when it moved. It tracks the
translatable data: a LingoHub release can still change how a format is rendered, and ARB embeds a generation timestamp -
re-export after a release when byte identity matters. Null for a file
without languages.

items.description: Languages without a form of their own that use this preferred form, e.g. `de-AT` using the `de` form. Empty for every other form.

language_code.description: Language of the form; null for the forms of an untranslatable term.

match_expression.description: The regular expression a `CUSTOM` matching uses.

term_id.description: Unique identifier of the term the form belongs to.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the form was last updated.

TermFormType.description: Lexical type of a term form.

TermType.description:
Whether a term is translated:
  - TRANSLATABLE: the term is translated; each of its forms belongs to a language.
  - UNTRANSLATABLE: the term stays as it is in every language (a brand or product name); its forms have no language.

Text.description: Current variants and workflow state of one shared segment in one stack language, source included. Changes affect every key of the segment.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the text was created.

id.description: Public identifier of this text.

is_source.description: Whether this is the stack's current source language.

language_code.description: Language code of this text.

segment_id.description: Public identifier of the shared segment.

text_updated_at.description: Last current-text insertion, update or deletion time; null before any current text change. Neither timestamp is a complete change feed.

updated_at.description: Persisted metadata update time of the text. Variant changes have a separate text_updated_at timestamp.

variants.description: Current text variants in position, device and plural-form order. Empty when no current text exists.

TextAction.description: Manual workflow action. Source texts support APPROVE and REOPEN; targets support all actions.

TextBulkItem.description: One ordered text mutation result. Only SUCCEEDED carries a text, Location and ETag. FAILED and UNKNOWN carry a problem. NOT_PROCESSED has no status or problem.

etag.description: ETag of the updated text representation, for subsequent conditional writes.

location.description: Canonical relative URL of a successfully updated text.

reference.description: Caller reference from this input item.

status.description: Single-item HTTP status: 200 on success, 4xx on rejection, 500 on an unknown outcome; null when not attempted.

TextBulkResult.description: Synchronous, non-paginated result with exactly one item per input in the same order. HTTP 200 does not imply every item succeeded. Commits are independent; stop and reconcile UNKNOWN outcomes before new work.

data.description: Ordered per-item outcomes, including items not attempted after an unexpected failure.

TextCollection.description: A cursor-paginated list of Text objects.

data.description: The list of items in this page.

has_more.description: True if more items exist after this page. Iterate by repeating the request with the cursor query parameter set to next_cursor until has_more is false.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor token pointing past the last item of this page. Null on the last page. Pass it unchanged via the cursor query parameter to request the next page.

TextDirection.description:
The writing direction of a locale:
  - LTR: left-to-right (e.g. English, German)
  - RTL: right-to-left (e.g. Arabic, Hebrew)

TextStage.description:
The high-level workflow stage that groups one or more `TextStatus` values:
  - `NOT_READY` — blocked segments
  - `NEEDS_EDIT` — new, draft, stale or rejected segments
  - `NEEDS_REVIEW` — AI-translated, translated, QA-passed or QA-flagged segments
  - `DONE` — approved or not-translatable segments

TextStatus.description: The workflow status of texts in a given language. Each status belongs to exactly one `TextStage` (see the `stage` grouping in the status counts).

TextUpdateMode.description: When an import may update an existing text.

TextVariant.description: One current variant of a text. History and suggestions are separate.

content.description: Current text content, including any placeholders or markup.

position.description: Stored position of this variant within the text.

TransferContentIntegration.description: Request body to pull or push resources through the existing content integration.

language_codes.description: Language selection from the current default branch. Null or an empty list uses all eligible languages according to the provider workflow. Duplicate codes are rejected.

items.description: Language selection from the current default branch. Null or an empty list uses all eligible languages according to the provider workflow. Duplicate codes are rejected.

resource_ids.description: Resource selection in the project's current default branch. Null or an empty list selects all eligible resources, preserving the provider workflow. Duplicate identities are rejected.

items.description: Public id that is created from the type prefix of the corresponding resource and its UUID. I.e : For a resource container, a valid value would be : rc_0197c8f2-5a6b-7cde-8f12-3456789abcde

TransitionText.description: Request body to apply a manual workflow action to a text without replacing its variants.

TransitionTextsBulk.description: Request body to transition 1–150 branch-selected texts with independent commits. References and text identities must be unique.

items.description: Ordered items. Structural, duplicate-target and condition syntax validation completes before writes.

TranslateLina.description: Request body to translate plain texts without a project. At most 16,384 source characters in total.

source_language_code.description: Language code that uniquely identifies a locale. Valid examples would be 'en', 'en-GB', 'de', 'de-DE' etc. according to [ISO 639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639_language_codes).

target_language_code.description: Language code that uniquely identifies a locale. Valid examples would be 'en', 'en-GB', 'de', 'de-DE' etc. according to [ISO 639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639_language_codes).

texts.description: One to ten uniquely keyed plain texts.

TranslateLinaText.description: Request body to translate one caller-keyed plain text.

key.description: Caller-selected unique key for correlating this result.

text.description: Plain source text. Whitespace is preserved; no project format or placeholders are inferred.

UpdateBranch.description: Request body to partially update a branch (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Only fields present in the request body are changed; an omitted `name` is left unchanged. `name` cannot be null.

UpdateContextImage.description: Request body to partially update a context image (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Only fields present in the request body are changed; omitted fields are left unchanged and an explicit `description: null` clears the description. `name` cannot be null.

description.description: Description of what the image shows. An explicit null clears it.
description.example: Screenshot of the checkout screen showing the payment options.

name.description: Display name of the context image.

UpdateGlossary.description: Request body to partially update a glossary (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged; neither field can be set to null. A provided `language_codes` list replaces the configured languages.

language_codes.description: Codes of the languages available in the glossary. Replaces the configured set.

UpdateIntegrationAuthentication.description: Request body to rename a stored authentication. Omitted name leaves it unchanged; null is not accepted. Credentials and provider lifecycle are unchanged.

UpdateKey.description: Request body to update the display name of a key. Source imports may overwrite the name under existing import settings. The key and its position are unchanged.

name.description: Display name of the key. Omission preserves it; null is not accepted.

UpdateLabel.description: Request body to partially update a label (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged. `ai_context` may be set to null to clear it; `name` and `color` cannot be null.

ai_context.description: Context describing the label's meaning to AI features (e.g., LINA translation agents).
ai_context.example: Short, catchy texts for marketing campaigns

color.description: Hex color code of the label (e.g., #FF5733).

name.description: Display name of the label. Must be unique within the workspace (case-insensitive).

UpdateLina.description: Request body to partially update a LINA. Omitted fields stay unchanged; null clears nullable fields.

is_restricted.description: Restrict use to selected stacks; false clears stored restrictions.

language_engine_overrides.description: Replacement per-language engine overrides. Empty clears all overrides.

restricted_stack_ids.description: Replacement stack restrictions. Empty means no stack is allowed when restricted; ignored when unrestricted.

style_guide_id.description: Workspace style guide; null clears it.

UpdateLinaContext.description: Request body to partially update LINA context inputs.

UpdateMember.description: Request body to update a non-owner workspace member's role while preserving explicit stack assignments.

workspace_role_id.description: Existing non-owner workspace role. Omission preserves the current role; null is not allowed.

UpdateProject.description: Request body to partially update a LingoHub project (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged. `ai_context` and `website` may be set to null to clear them; `name` and `color` cannot be null.

ai_context.description: The AI context of the project.

color.description: Hex color code of the project icon.

UpdateProjectIntegrationSettings.description: Request body to partially update the integration settings of a project (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged; neither field can be null.

is_removed_language_deletion_enabled.description: Whether a sync deletes languages the integration no longer reports. The source language is never deleted. Only Contentful, HubSpot, Storyblok, Stripo and Zendesk integrations read this setting; Git and Crisp integrations never delete languages.

is_removed_resource_deletion_enabled.description: Whether a Git repository pull deletes files the repository no longer contains. Only Git integrations read this setting; the other integrations always delete resources a sync no longer reports.

UpdateProjectLanguage.description: Request body to partially update a project language (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged. Both `file_slug` and `fallback_language_code` may be set to null to clear them.

fallback_language_code.description: Language code used as a fallback when a translation is missing for this language.

file_slug.description: Custom slug used when generating resource file names for this language.

UpdateResource.description: Request body to partially update a resource (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Only fields present in the request body are changed; omitted fields are left unchanged. Renaming the `path` also moves the resource and its sub-resources within the branch.

language_code_separator.description: New separator used between the file name and the language code. Cannot be blank.

path.description: New full path of the resource within the branch: relative, segments separated by `/`, the last one naming the resource. No empty or `..` segment, no segment longer than 255 characters. A file path must retain `%{locale}` somewhere in the path. When its basename combines `%{locale}` with other text, use `%{language_code_separator}` as the separator, for example `messages%{language_code_separator}%{locale}.json`. Keep an extension allowed by the resource's format. A folder path does not need a locale placeholder.

UpdateSegment.description: Request body to partially update shared segment metadata. Omitted fields remain unchanged; nullable strings may be cleared. Changes affect every key of the segment.

ai_context.description: Context for AI translation; null clears it.

description.description: Shared translator-facing description; null clears it.

is_not_translatable.description: Whether this shared segment is excluded from translation. Attribution and reason are derived by the server.

is_plural.description: Whether the segment uses plural forms. Every active file format must support the change. Becoming singular retains current OTHER-form texts and removes all other current plural forms across all languages.

label_ids.description: Replaces shared label assignments with existing labels in this workspace. Empty clears all labels. At most 150 distinct labels.

UpdateStack.description: Request body to partially update a LingoHub stack (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged; `name` and `color` cannot be null, a null `ai_context` or `lina_id` removes it.

ai_context.description: Context that tells LINA what the stack is about, given with the project's own.

color.description: Hex color code of the stack icon.

lina_id.description: LINA of the workspace to assign to the stack; null removes the assignment. The stack languages keep their `lina_role`.

UpdateStackLanguage.description: Request body to partially update a stack language (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged; `lina_role` cannot be null.

UpdateStackMember.description: Request body to merge an existing stack assignment's role and explicit language permissions.

language_permissions.description: Map entries are merged, not replaced. Omission or an empty map preserves explicit rows; a null value removes that locale's explicit row. The map itself cannot be null. This describes stored configuration, not effective access.

stack_role_id.description: Existing non-owner stack role. Omission preserves it; null is invalid.

UpdateStyleGuide.description: Request body to partially update a LingoHub style guide (PATCH, JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged. `name` and `rules` cannot be null; `ai_context` and `audience_description` may be set to null to clear them, and each rule inside `rules` may be set to null to reset it to `NOT_SPECIFIED`.

ai_context.description: Additional context provided to the AI to guide translation style and tone.
ai_context.example: Translate in a friendly and approachable tone suitable for a SaaS product.

audience_description.description: Description of the target audience for this style guide.
audience_description.example: Software developers and technical users familiar with localization workflows.

name.description: Display name of the style guide.

UpdateStyleGuideRules.description: Style rules to change (JSON merge-patch): omitted rules are left unchanged, a rule set to null is reset to NOT_SPECIFIED.

UpdateTerm.description: Request body to partially update a term (JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged. The forms have their own endpoints.

ai_context.description: Context for AI translation. Null clears it.
ai_context.example: Final step of the purchase flow.

UpdateTermForm.description: Request body to partially update a term form (JSON merge-patch). Omitted fields are left unchanged, null clears a nullable field. The language of a form cannot change: add a form in the other language and delete this one instead.

inherited_by.description: Languages without a form of their own that use this form. Replaces the current list; only for the preferred form of a translatable term. A language removed from the list keeps a copy of the form.

match_expression.description: The regular expression a `CUSTOM` matching uses. Null clears it.

UpdateText.description: Request body to update the variants of a shared text. Omission leaves the variants unchanged; null is invalid; an empty array clears them. Changes affect every key of the segment.

is_minor_update.description: Uses existing minor-edit status automation behavior. Omission or null means false. Only valid with variants.

key_id.description: Active key selecting the project settings and automations. Required with variants; changes still affect every key of the segment.

variants.description: Replaces all current variants in array order. At most 1,000 entries and 1,048,576 UTF-16 code units in total.

UpdateTextsBulk.description: Request body to update 1–150 branch-selected texts with independent commits. References and text identities must be unique.

items.description: Ordered items. Structural, duplicate-target and condition syntax validation completes before writes.

UpdateWebhookEndpoint.description: Request body to partially update a webhook endpoint. Omitted fields stay unchanged; null clears description or scope. Switching scope requires explicitly clearing the previous scope. Event types replace the complete subscription list.

event_types.description: Replacement public event names, or ["*"] for all subscribable events.

project_id.description: Project scope in this workspace; null clears it.

stack_id.description: Stack scope in this workspace; null clears it.

UpdateWorkspaceApiKey.description: Request body to partially update active workspace-managed key metadata without changing its permissions or ownership.

name.description: Display name, unique among workspace-managed keys.

UploadLimits.description: Limits enforced on multipart uploads and ZIP extraction; sizes are bytes.

archive_extensions.description: Archive extensions with a leading dot, matched case-insensitively. DOCX/PPTX are files, not upload archives.

items.description: Archive extensions with a leading dot, matched case-insensitively. DOCX/PPTX are files, not upload archives.

max_archive_entries.description: Maximum ZIP entries, counting hidden, empty and directory entries before filtering.

max_archive_entry_bytes.description: Maximum inflated bytes of one ZIP entry; project file limits also apply.

max_archive_total_bytes.description: Maximum total inflated ZIP bytes before filtering hidden or empty entries.

max_file_parts.description: The import endpoint accepts one file part: a single file or a ZIP archive.

max_multipart_file_bytes.description: Runtime maximum size of the uploaded part; null means unlimited.

max_request_bytes.description: Runtime maximum size of the whole multipart request, including boundaries and form fields; null means unlimited.

mime_types.description: Accepted declared MIME types. Empty means unconstrained: V2 validates filename extension and content, not a MIME allowlist.

items.description: Accepted declared MIME types. Empty means unconstrained: V2 validates filename extension and content, not a MIME allowlist.

UsageStatus.description:

  - ADMITTED: an accepted alternative form.

info.description:
> **Beta:** API V2 is in beta. Endpoints, request and response fields, and behavior can still change. Use the LingoHub CLI (`lh-cli`) where possible: it is updated together with the API. If you call the HTTP API directly, be prepared to update your integration when V2 changes.

The LingoHub V2 API provides programmatic access to your localization workflow. Use it to manage workspaces, projects, resources, translations, and more.

## Authentication

All requests require a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header. API keys can be created in the LingoHub workspace settings and use the `lh-api_` prefix.

```
Authorization: Bearer lh-api_your_api_key_here
```

## Pagination

List endpoints use cursor pagination via the `cursor` and `limit` query parameters (`limit` defaults to 20, maximum 100). Each response contains the returned items in `data`, a `has_more` flag, and an opaque `next_cursor` token that is null on the last page. To iterate a collection, repeat the request with `cursor` set to the previous response's `next_cursor` until `has_more` is false. Keep all other query parameters identical while iterating — a cursor is bound to the collection (parent resource), the filters, and the sort order it was created under and is rejected with an `invalid_cursor` error otherwise. Total counts are intentionally not provided; items created or deleted before the cursor position are not revisited during an iteration.

## Filtering

Lists take a `filter` query parameter: URL-encoded JSON that selects the items to return (`where`) and orders them (`sort`). `where` holds exactly one `_and` or `_or` with an array of clauses; a clause is a nested `_and`/`_or`, or a field with exactly one operator. Fields are named `<object_type>[<field>]` after the list's items, e.g. `project[name]`, and compare the values the responses show. Each list documents its fields, their operators and values, and which of them sort, in its `filter` parameter and its schema (`ProjectFilter`, ...). A field, operator or value a list does not support answers `400 invalid_filter`, with an error pointing into the filter and naming what is supported there.

### Example

```json
{
  "where": {
    "_and": [
      { "project[name]": { "_icontains": "app" } },
      {
        "_or": [
          { "project[type]": { "_eq": "STANDARD_JSON" } },
          { "project[created_at]": { "_gte": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" } }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "sort": ["-project[created_at]"]
}
```

An unknown value is answered with where it is and what the field accepts:

```json
{
  "status": 400,
  "code": "invalid_filter",
  "errors": [
    {
      "parameter": "filter",
      "pointer": "#/where/_and/1/_or/0/project[type]/_eq",
      "code": "enum",
      "detail": "'JSON' is not a value of 'project[type]'. Values: ANDROID_XML, IOS_STRINGS, ..."
    }
  ]
}
```

## Rate limiting

Requests are rate limited per API key and per workspace (aggregate across all of its keys). Exceeding either limit returns `429 rate_limit_exceeded` with a `Retry-After` header stating the seconds to wait before retrying. Responses to authenticated requests additionally carry the structured `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers (IETF draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers): `RateLimit-Policy` lists the applied policies with their request quota `q` per window of `w` seconds, and `RateLimit` reports the policy currently closest to rejection with the requests remaining right now (`r`) and the seconds until the full quota is available again (`t`). Use them to pace request rates proactively instead of backing off on 429 — but treat them as advisory: they are absent when the request fails authentication or the limiter state is momentarily unknown.

## Errors

All error responses follow the RFC 9457 Problem Details format with additional `code` and `request_id` fields for machine-readable error handling and support requests, and an additional `errors` field for handling multiple validation errors at once.

The field-level validation errors return a JSON pointer to the problem value, a detail description, and a machine-readable code. For more information, see RFC 9457 Section 3 §7.

delete.description: Revokes the personal API key this request is made with, as its owner deleting it in LingoHub would: the key is deactivated, its metadata and history remain, and later requests with it fail with 401 `revoked_api_key`. Command-line clients use this to sign out. Workspace-managed keys cannot revoke themselves and get 403 `insufficient_permissions`; a workspace administrator revokes them with `deleteWorkspaceApiKey`. Optional If-Match uses the validator of `getApiKey`; a stale one returns 412. Requires a valid personal API key.

parameters.description: Optional precondition. Send the quoted ETag from a GET of this resource. The mutation only runs if a strong tag matches the current representation, checked under the write lock. A comma-separated list is allowed; '*' requires an existing representation. Weak tags never match. Omit this header for an unconditional write. For an action, use the ETag from GET of the target resource, without the action suffix. A stale tag returns 412; read the current state before retrying.

get.description: Returns retained key metadata across this workspace with SQL cursor pagination, including workspace-managed and user-owned keys of all scopes and retained deactivated keys. Credentials and permission payloads are excluded. Stack/member/user identity filters select stored response references, not effective access. Null or unavailable references never match these filters, including negative comparisons. Identity arrays must be nonempty; these fields are not sortable. GET /v2/api-key separately describes the calling key and its current effective permissions. Requires workspace-level API access view permission.

parameters.description:
Filters and sorts the list: URL-encoded JSON of the schema `WorkspaceApiKeyFilter`. `where` holds exactly one `_and` or `_or` with an array of clauses; a clause is another `_and`/`_or` or a field with exactly one operator. `sort` lists fields with `+` (ascending) or `-` (descending). An unsupported field, operator or value answers `400 invalid_filter` with a pointer into the filter.

| Field | Type | Operators | Sort |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_api_key[created_at]` | timestamp | `_eq` `_lt` `_gt` `_lte` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` | yes |
| `workspace_api_key[deactivation_reason]` | EXPIRATION_DATE \| WORKSPACE_USER_REMOVED \| STACK_DELETED \| MANUAL_REVOCATION \| SELF_SERVICE_DISABLED | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `workspace_api_key[description]` | text | `_eq` `_ne` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_blank` `_nblank` | – |
| `workspace_api_key[id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `workspace_api_key[is_deactivated]` | boolean | `_true` `_false` | – |
| `workspace_api_key[management_mode]` | WORKSPACE_MANAGED \| USER_OWNED | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `workspace_api_key[member_id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `workspace_api_key[name]` | text | `_eq` `_ne` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_blank` `_nblank` | yes |
| `workspace_api_key[scope]` | WORKSPACE \| STACK \| USER | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `workspace_api_key[stack_id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `workspace_api_key[updated_at]` | timestamp | `_eq` `_lt` `_gt` `_lte` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` | yes |
| `workspace_api_key[user_id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |

post.description: Creates a WORKSPACE, STACK or assigned-USER workspace-managed key through the existing key lifecycle. Scope and target are immutable. Configured expiration is inclusive through that UTC day. Initial stack permissions receive the requested default stack levels. Returns a one-time token and Location of token-free metadata. Credentials are excluded from logs and replay storage; a keyed repeat returns idempotency_outcome_unknown (409) without re-executing while retained. Inspect inventory before deliberately recovering an uncertain result. User-owned self-service keys are not provisioned here. Requires workspace-level API access management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort duplicate suppression of this one-time response. The original successful response is returned to the caller but never retained in API log bodies or Redis replay results. Only an unresolved reservation is retained for 24 hours by default; a matching retry returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without repeating the operation or revealing its secret. A concurrent request returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use`; a changed request returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution. A 4xx rejection releases its reservation; interruption after execution or loss of the success response requires inspection and a deliberate new operation. Redis expiry/eviction or explicit server-side disabling removes protection; this is not durable exactly-once execution. Use the target GET to inspect current metadata and obtain its validator, then a new key only when intentionally rotating again.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

post.description: Rotates an active workspace-managed key and returns its new credential only in this original response. Existing tokens stop authenticating; key configuration, scope and expiration remain. Requires current workspace API access management permission. User-owned targets and inactive keys are forbidden, preserving the existing administration policy. Missing/foreign keys are 404. Optional If-Match uses the current inventory GET validator under the key lock. The response is excluded from API log bodies and Redis replay results, carries Cache-Control no-store and no ETag. A retained Idempotency-Key returns idempotency_outcome_unknown (409) without re-executing; Redis loss/expiry is not durable exactly-once delivery. A lost response may require deliberate new rotation with a separately authorized credential. Inventory GET never reveals tokens. Self-rotation invalidates the caller's old token after the response.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort duplicate suppression of this one-time response. The original successful response is returned to the caller but never retained in API log bodies or Redis replay results. Only an unresolved reservation is retained for 24 hours by default; a matching retry returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without repeating the operation or revealing its secret. A concurrent request returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use`; a changed request returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution. A 4xx rejection releases its reservation; interruption after execution or loss of the success response requires inspection and a deliberate new operation. Redis expiry/eviction or explicit server-side disabling removes protection; this is not durable exactly-once execution. Use the target GET to inspect current metadata and obtain its validator, then a new key only when intentionally rotating again.

delete.description: Logically deletes a retained backup and its terminal restore polling records through the shared lifecycle. Snapshot storage cleanup is durably recorded in the same transaction and retried asynchronously; 204 does not assert that storage cleanup has finished. Queued/running capture or restore work returns 409 backup_in_use. Optional If-Match uses getBackup. Requires current project settings-management permission. Audit actors remain permanent.

schema.description: Public id composed of the resource type prefix and its UUID.

parameters.description: Optional precondition. Send the quoted ETag from a GET of this resource. The mutation only runs if a strong tag matches the current representation, checked under the write lock. A comma-separated list is allowed; '*' requires an existing representation. Weak tags never match. Omit this header for an unconditional write. For an action, use the ETag from GET of the target resource, without the action suffix. A stale tag returns 412; read the current state before retrying.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

post.description: Schedules a snapshot of the ready branch. Returns 202 with its initial metadata; poll the Location URL while QUEUED or PROCESSING. Capture runs later through the existing resource-sync read lock, so created_at is scheduling time. SUCCEEDED confirms completion. Use the same Idempotency-Key after a lost response to recover the originally scheduled backup. Requires branch-level settings management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description:
Filters and sorts the list: URL-encoded JSON of the schema `ExportFilter`. `where` holds exactly one `_and` or `_or` with an array of clauses; a clause is another `_and`/`_or` or a field with exactly one operator. `sort` lists fields with `+` (ascending) or `-` (descending). An unsupported field, operator or value answers `400 invalid_filter` with a pointer into the filter.

| Field | Type | Operators | Sort |
|---|---|---|---|
| `export[created_at]` | timestamp | `_eq` `_lt` `_gt` `_lte` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` | yes |
| `export[id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `export[status]` | QUEUED \| PROCESSING \| SUCCEEDED \| PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED \| FAILED \| CANCELLED \| SKIPPED | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `export[trigger]` | API_V2 \| API_V1 \| API_V1_SINGLE_FILE \| DOWNLOAD \| DOWNLOAD_MULTIPLE \| GIT_PUSH \| GIT_PUSH_MULTIPLE \| DISTRIBUTION_RELEASE \| BACKUP \| XLIFF \| CSV \| FIGMA \| ZENDESK_PUSH \| STORYBLOK_PUSH \| CONTENTFUL_PUSH \| HUBSPOT_PUSH \| STRIPO_PUSH \| CRISP_HELPDESK_PUSH \| PACKAGES \| ZENDESK_SELECTED \| ZENDESK_ALL | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |

post.description: Uploads a file and imports it into the branch as an asynchronous job (multipart upload, plain form fields). Send the file in the `file` field. A file whose name ends in `.zip` is an archive: every file inside it is imported under its path in the archive, skipping hidden files (names starting with a dot) and empty entries. Any other file is imported as the single file it is, including documents such as DOCX or PPTX that are ZIP containers internally. `path` is the folder the file, or every file of the archive, is imported into; without it they are imported at the project root. `language_code` is the language of the file, or of every file of the archive; without it, the language is detected from each file's name and path. Returns 202 with the import; poll it at the URL in the `Location` header while QUEUED or PROCESSING. SUCCEEDED is full success; PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED means some work failed. Inspect status_details and entries before retrying failed or partial work. Requires branch-level resource management permission. Use the same Idempotency-Key when retrying an upload whose response was lost to recover the original import instead of scheduling another one.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. post.description: Schedules the given target languages for addition to the branch. The languages are created by an import, which the job carries; poll the import (the URL in the `Location` header) while `QUEUED` or `PROCESSING`. Inspect `status_details` and entries for `FAILED` or `PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED` outcomes. Already-configured languages are `SKIPPED` entries with the `ALREADY_EXISTS` code; they do not prevent new languages from being created. Requires project-level languages management permission; the import, its entries and its logs can be read with languages view permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: Optional precondition. Send the quoted ETag from a GET of this resource. The mutation only runs if a strong tag matches the current representation, checked under the write lock. A comma-separated list is allowed; '*' requires an existing representation. Weak tags never match. Omit this header for an unconditional write. For an action, use the ETag from GET of the target resource, without the action suffix. A stale tag returns 412; read the current state before retrying.
parameters.name: If-Match

post.description: Applies named workflow actions to existing shared texts selected through active keys in this branch. Preserves the single-operation source/target and workflow permission rules; no arbitrary status writes. Actions affect every key of the segment. Accepts 1–150 items with distinct references and text IDs. Structural validation precedes writes; each item commits independently. Optional per-item if_match is checked under mutation locks; aggregate If-Match is rejected. HTTP 200 can contain failures. Unexpected failures stop later items with UNKNOWN/NOT_PROCESSED outcomes; reconcile before new work. Idempotency-Key replays the entire retained result, including failures; corrected batches use a new key. Redis expiry/loss or disabled idempotency can permit execution again. Requires stack-level text management and segment, key and resource view permissions for each selected context.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

Optional If-Match checks the complete metadata GET validator under current ancestry, distribution and release locks. Supports Idempotency-Key. parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

post.description: Cancels an unclaimed queued UPLOAD, XLIFF or CSV import atomically with worker scheduling. The request has no body. An already-cancelled supported import is a no-op. A queued response is not a cancellation guarantee: the worker may claim it before this request acquires its lock. Active or completed work and other import types return import_not_cancellable; active work is never interrupted and applied translations are never rolled back. Remaining ready entries become SKIPPED, uploaded data follows existing retention, and the original import actor is retained with separate cancellation audit attribution. Optional If-Match checks the current getImport representation under locks. Supports Idempotency-Key. Requires stack-level resource management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional precondition. Send the quoted ETag from a GET of this resource. The mutation only runs if a strong tag matches the current representation, checked under the write lock. A comma-separated list is allowed; '*' requires an existing representation. Weak tags never match. Omit this header for an unconditional write. For an action, use the ETag from GET of the target resource, without the action suffix. A stale tag returns 412; read the current state before retrying.

This list cannot be sorted. An unsupported field, operator or value answers `400 invalid_filter` with a pointer into the filter.

| Field | Type | Operators |
|---|---|---|
| `import_entry[file_path]` | text | `_eq` `_ne` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_blank` `_nblank` |
| `import_entry[file_size_bytes]` | integer | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` `_gt` `_lt` `_gte` `_lte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` |
| `import_entry[language_code]` | language code | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_blank` `_nblank` `_gt` |
| `import_entry[resource_id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` |
| `import_entry[status]` | QUEUED \| PROCESSING \| SUCCEEDED \| FAILED \| SKIPPED \| UNCHANGED | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` |

post.description: Stores manual credentials through the existing setup of the provider named by `provider`; the workspace integration of that provider must be available. Git hosts store the credentials without a remote check, so ACTIVE is the stored lifecycle, not proof of connectivity; content systems validate them with the provider first. GitHub authentications come from installing the GitHub app (getGitHubInstallationLink) instead. No project or synchronization is created. Returns credential-free metadata and its Location. Use the same Idempotency-Key for the same intended submission; after an uncertain response, list the authentications before resubmitting. Requires workspace-level integration management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

post.description: Creates a new project in a new private stack using the existing provider workflow, then queues its initial synchronization. Project creation and job submission commit together; provider work runs asynchronously and can partially succeed. The import identifies the new default branch; retrieve that branch to find its project. No live-provider preflight occurs. Requires workspace-level stack management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

| `invitation[invitee_name]` | text | `_eq` `_ne` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_blank` `_nblank` | – |

post.description: Renews a retained pending or expired EMAIL invitation for the existing seven-day period and reuses the existing email or user-notification workflow. Accepted or declined invitations cannot be resent. Workspace/stack owner invitations must be managed outside the API. The existing token, inviter and assignment are preserved; bearer tokens and acceptance links are never returned. Optional If-Match uses GET invitation's current validator, including computed expiry status. A retained successful Idempotency-Key replay does not extend expiry or dispatch again. An external delivery may have occurred before a failed response; Redis does not provide durable exactly-once delivery. Requires current workspace members-management permission.

schema.description: Public id composed of the resource type prefix and its UUID.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: Optional precondition. Send the quoted ETag from a GET of this resource. The mutation only runs if a strong tag matches the current representation, checked under the write lock. A comma-separated list is allowed; '*' requires an existing representation. Weak tags never match. Omit this header for an unconditional write. For an action, use the ETag from GET of the target resource, without the action suffix. A stale tag returns 412; read the current state before retrying.

delete.description: Removes the stored stack assignment from a pending or expired retained EMAIL invitation without deleting the invitation, changing its workspace role, notifying the invitee or changing existing memberships. GET then reports NOT_CONFIGURED; an absent assignment is a no-op. Accepted, declined, unavailable and owner invitations are protected. If-Match compares the current assignment representation. LINK invitations are excluded. Requires workspace-level members management and settings-management permission on every assigned stack.

post.description: Returns synchronous results without creating project segments. Reuses LINA routing, language overrides, glossary/style-guide/memory context, cache and credit charging through the interactive provider path. At most ten inputs and 16384 source characters; partial or failed provider work returns explicit per-input outcomes in the 200 body. Results are not retained as a pollable job. A timeout has an uncertain outcome; inspect idempotency guidance before retrying. Restricted, disabled or archived LINAs cannot execute without project scope. Requires workspace-level AI translation management permission.

schema.description: Public id composed of the resource type prefix and its UUID.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description:
Filters and sorts the list: URL-encoded JSON of the schema `LinguisticEngineFilter`. `where` holds exactly one `_and` or `_or` with an array of clauses; a clause is another `_and`/`_or` or a field with exactly one operator. `sort` lists fields with `+` (ascending) or `-` (descending). An unsupported field, operator or value answers `400 invalid_filter` with a pointer into the filter.

| Field | Type | Operators | Sort |
|---|---|---|---|
| `linguistic_engine[created_at]` | timestamp | `_eq` `_lt` `_gt` `_lte` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` | yes |
| `linguistic_engine[id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `linguistic_engine[model]` | MT_GOOGLE_TRANSLATE_V3 \| MT_DEEPL_TRANSLATE_V1 \| MT_AWS_TRANSLATE \| AI_GPT_5_4 \| AI_GPT_5_4_MINI \| AI_GPT_5_4_NANO \| AI_GPT_5_6_SOL \| AI_GPT_5_6_TERRA \| AI_GPT_5_6_LUNA \| AI_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH \| AI_GEMINI_2_5_PRO \| AI_GEMINI_3_6_FLASH \| AI_GEMINI_3_5_FLASH_LITE \| AI_CLAUDE_OPUS_4_7 \| AI_CLAUDE_SONNET_4_6 \| AI_CLAUDE_HAIKU_4_5 \| AI_CLAUDE_OPUS_5 \| AI_CLAUDE_SONNET_5 \| AI_MISTRAL_LARGE_3 \| AI_MISTRAL_SMALL_4 \| AI_MISTRAL_MEDIUM_3_5 | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `linguistic_engine[updated_at]` | timestamp | `_eq` `_lt` `_gt` `_lte` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` | yes |

get.description: Returns a cursor-paginated list of projects in the workspace that the API key belongs to. Results are limited to projects the API key has permission to view. Use `filter` to search projects; iterate by passing `next_cursor` of the previous page via the `cursor` query parameter until `has_more` is false. Requires workspace-level general view permission.

parameters.description:
Filters and sorts the list: URL-encoded JSON of the schema `ProjectFilter`. `where` holds exactly one `_and` or `_or` with an array of clauses; a clause is another `_and`/`_or` or a field with exactly one operator. `sort` lists fields with `+` (ascending) or `-` (descending). An unsupported field, operator or value answers `400 invalid_filter` with a pointer into the filter.

| Field | Type | Operators | Sort |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project[created_at]` | timestamp | `_eq` `_lt` `_gt` `_lte` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` | yes |
| `project[id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `project[name]` | text | `_eq` `_ne` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_blank` `_nblank` | yes |
| `project[stack_id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `project[type]` | ANDROID_XML \| IOS_STRINGS \| IOS_STRINGS_CATALOG \| STANDARD_PROPERTIES \| GETTEXT_PO \| WINDOWS_RESX \| QT_LINGUIST_TS \| DEFINE_PHP \| STANDARD_INI \| STANDARD_ARB \| RAILS_YAML \| SYMFONY_YAML \| STANDARD_JSON \| ANGULAR_TRANSLATE_JSON \| CHROME_I18N_JSON \| GO_I18N_JSON \| I18NEXT_JSON \| REACT_INTL_JSON \| STANDARD_CSV \| SINGLE_LANGUAGE_CSV \| KEY_VALUE_CSV \| STANDARD_XLIFF \| STANDARD_XLIFF_2 \| STANDARD_TXT \| TWINE_TXT \| STANDARD_MARKDOWN \| STANDARD_HTML \| FIGMA \| ZENDESK \| STORYBLOK \| STORYBLOK_JSON \| CONTENTFUL \| INTERCOM \| SUBTITLE_SRT \| SUBTITLE_VTT \| HUBSPOT \| STRIPO \| CRISP_HELPDESK \| DOCUMENT \| VUE_I18N_JSON | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `project[updated_at]` | timestamp | `_eq` `_lt` `_gt` `_lte` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` | yes |

post.description: Creates a new localization project in the workspace that the API key belongs to. The project type determines the resource file format used for translations (e.g., 'ANDROID_XML', 'IOS_STRINGS', 'STANDARD_JSON'). A source language and at least one target language are required. Requires workspace-level stack management permission. Optional `stack_id` selects an existing stack and also requires stack-level settings and language management permissions.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.
