delete.description: Permanently deletes the project identified by the given ID and all its associated data, including segments and texts. Deletion is processed asynchronously - the project is immediately marked for removal and cleaned up in the background. This action cannot be undone. Requires stack-level settings management permission.

put.description: Enables or replaces the complete UTC schedule and nonempty project-branch selection using the existing scheduler. Equal settings do not write or move the next execution. A changed schedule or selection follows the existing writer, which recalculates the next execution; saving does not start a backup now. Retained snapshots, restores and already queued work remain. Use DELETE to disable. Requires project settings management; use GET for the full conditional validator.

post.description: Creates a new branch in the given project. When `starting_point_branch_id` is provided, the new branch is seeded with a copy of that branch's texts asynchronously. 201 means the branch exists, not that copying finished. Poll the branch at Location every two seconds until initialization_status is SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED or SKIPPED. initialization_error explains terminal failures. Metadata edits and deletion remain available while pending; imports, exports, language changes and making it the default require SUCCEEDED. Requires project-level settings management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. post.description: Uploads a new context image to the given project (multipart upload, plain form fields). Send the image in the `file` field and the `language_code` of the UI text shown in it. Without `rendered_strings`, the image is run through OCR text-detection and matched against the project's segments in that language; `auto_connect_suggestions` (default true) controls whether those matches are auto-connected or left as suggestions for manual review. Segments can also be attached explicitly via the attach endpoint. Requires project-level context-image management permission. Use the same Idempotency-Key when retrying an upload whose response was lost to recover the original context image. Optional `capture_key` scopes replacements to the default branch language. Equal hashes leave metadata, links and quota unchanged. Changed captures count as one upload, rebuild all their links and leave other images untouched. `rendered_strings` is a JSON array part and skips OCR, including `[]`.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. put.description: Replaces all project export defaults used when transfer workflow settings are resolved. Stored job-specific overrides are not rewritten; already queued jobs without overrides may use the new defaults when resolved. Every field is required. Equal values write nothing. Optional If-Match uses the complete corresponding GET representation under current project/settings locks. Current permissions are rechecked after waits. put.description: Replaces all project import defaults used when transfer workflow settings are resolved. Stored job-specific overrides are not rewritten; already queued jobs without overrides may use the new defaults when resolved. Every field is required. Equal values write nothing. Optional If-Match uses the complete corresponding GET representation under current project/settings locks. Current permissions are rechecked after waits. Returns no PUT ETag; GET again for the next validator. Actual changes retain settings audit, content-version and cache invalidation behavior. Requires project-level settings management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

Projects, branches, translations, shared authentication and retained import/export history remain. Remote webhook cleanup is best effort; this operation does not cancel in-flight jobs or retract provider writes. Optional If-Match validates the complete current getProjectGitIntegration representation under locks. Missing or already disconnected integrations return 404. If authentication is rebound while acquiring locks, 409 conflict requires a fresh read before retrying. Requires current stack settings management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

put.description: Replaces all push defaults and message templates of an existing connection; connection, sync modes, schedules, filters and branching are unchanged. Every field is required. Equal values write nothing. Optional If-Match checks the complete GET representation under project/authentication/configuration locks with current permission rechecked. Actual changes record an audit/event and reset ON_COMPLETION evaluations for the existing settle window; other modes clear obsolete evaluations. ON_COMPLETION requires at least one automatic branch kind enabled. This stores configuration, without contacting the provider or promising push success. Jobs lacking explicit overrides may use these defaults when their worker resolves them, including already queued jobs. Existing job records are not rewritten. Placeholders are expanded and PR branch templates normalized by the push worker. The transformed PUT omits ETag; GET again for a validator. Requires project-level settings management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

post.description: Reconciles the configured provider selection and optionally imports newly discovered resources. The existing synchronization may delete local resources no longer present in the selected provider result. Uses the current default branch, matching the editor. Returns a pollable job; individual entries may succeed before another fails. Inspect the terminal status and entries before retrying. Requires project-level resource management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

post.description: Queues the existing project move workflow. Only the languages the project uses go along; the destination gains those it lacks. Memberships and language permissions are not copied, so a member of the source stack who is not on the destination can lose access to the project. Workspace-key grants the destination lacks are copied; existing destination grants win. A private source stack is removed and a private destination becomes shared. Public sources require a public destination. The project keeps its own segments; equal texts are not merged. The project runs the destination stack's automations (`getStackAutomationSettings`); its own are not kept. Poll Location for completion. Requires project-level and destination stack-level settings management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

Equal ordered definitions write nothing. Requires current project settings-management permission, rechecked after project/settings row-lock waits. Actual changes retain existing audit, file-language content-version and quality-metadata invalidation behavior. Generic placeholder conversion remains separate.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

post.description: Creates 1–150 keys of one file, each with its fresh shared segment, in input order with independent commits. Structural and aggregate validation completes before writes. Per-item domain failures do not undo previous successes. An unexpected failure stops later items and marks the attempted outcome UNKNOWN; reconcile by listing the file's keys before new work. Redis expiry/loss or disabled idempotency can permit re-execution; batches are never atomic. No aggregate If-Match is accepted. Single-language CSV independent cell creation is not supported; import complete rows. Requires stack-level segment management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

put.description: Replaces the complete ordered rule configuration of the stack through the existing automation writer. An empty list removes all rules. Existing keys preserve identity; unknown or absent keys receive new server keys. Family order, rule validation, plan quota and shared-segment behavior stay unchanged. Current referenced labels are locked before the settings row, matching existing deletion and merge order. Requires stack settings management permission.

parameters.description:
Filters and sorts the list: URL-encoded JSON of the schema `StackMemberFilter`. `where` holds exactly one `_and` or `_or` with an array of clauses; a clause is another `_and`/`_or` or a field with exactly one operator. `sort` lists fields with `+` (ascending) or `-` (descending). An unsupported field, operator or value answers `400 invalid_filter` with a pointer into the filter.

| Field | Type | Operators | Sort |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stack_member[created_at]` | timestamp | `_eq` `_lt` `_gt` `_lte` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` | yes |
| `stack_member[email]` | text | `_eq` `_ne` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_blank` `_nblank` | – |
| `stack_member[first_name]` | text | `_eq` `_ne` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_blank` `_nblank` | – |
| `stack_member[id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `stack_member[last_name]` | text | `_eq` `_ne` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_blank` `_nblank` | – |
| `stack_member[stack_role_id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `stack_member[updated_at]` | timestamp | `_eq` `_lt` `_gt` `_lte` `_gte` `_within` `_null` `_nnull` | yes |
| `stack_member[user_id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |

patch.description: Merge-patches an existing stack assignment. Configured rows do not represent effective inherited access. Optional If-Match uses the GET representation. Requires stack settings-management permission.

Inherited workspace access may exist independently of these rows.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional precondition. Send the quoted ETag from a GET of this resource. The mutation only runs if a strong tag matches the current representation, checked under the write lock. A comma-separated list is allowed; '*' requires an existing representation. Weak tags never match. Omit this header for an unconditional write. For an action, use the ETag from GET of the target resource, without the action suffix. A stale tag returns 412; read the current state before retrying.

get.description: Returns currently readable stack languages contributing to a segment task, newest identity first by default. Current task audience, workspace/key scope, segment-view and language-read permissions apply before pagination. Hidden tasks or segment tasks with no readable contributors return 404; visible non-segment tasks return an empty collection. Items expose no recipient identity, historical counts or private payload. Cursors bind to the caller, task, filter and sort. Requires workspace general view permission.

schema.description: Public id composed of the resource type prefix and its UUID.

parameters.description:
Filters and sorts the list: URL-encoded JSON of the schema `TaskContributorFilter`. `where` holds exactly one `_and` or `_or` with an array of clauses; a clause is another `_and`/`_or` or a field with exactly one operator. `sort` lists fields with `+` (ascending) or `-` (descending). An unsupported field, operator or value answers `400 invalid_filter` with a pointer into the filter.

| Field | Type | Operators | Sort |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task_contributor[is_source]` | boolean | `_true` `_false` | – |
| `task_contributor[language_code]` | language code | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` `_like` `_nlike` `_ilike` `_nilike` `_contains` `_ncontains` `_icontains` `_nicontains` `_starts` `_ends` `_blank` `_nblank` `_gt` | yes |
| `task_contributor[stack_id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |
| `task_contributor[stack_language_id]` | id | `_eq` `_ne` `_in` `_nin` | – |

get.description: Returns persisted segment-work counters for only the task contributors readable by this API key. Requires current task audience, stack segment view and language read access. Missing/hidden tasks or a segment task with no readable contributors return 404. Non-segment tasks or incomplete counter rows return explicit null counts. Known empty work returns zero. post.description: Skips an open, skippable task as SKIPPED. Parent checklist completion follows the existing domain rules. The request has no body. Optional If-Match checks the complete task GET representation under a row lock. Supports Idempotency-Key; completed retries still check current audience access. Requires workspace-level general view permission and the task's current audience permission.

schema.description: Public id composed of the resource type prefix and its UUID.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional precondition. Send the quoted ETag from a GET of this resource. Weak tags never match. Omit this header for an unconditional write. For an action, use the ETag from GET of the target resource, without the action suffix. A stale tag returns 412; read the current state before retrying.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

post.description: Creates an enabled endpoint with the existing webhook validation and workspace API-access authority. Returns its identity and signing secret once; Location identifies the ordinary endpoint GET, which never discloses the secret. The original response is excluded from API log bodies and Redis replay results, has Cache-Control: no-store and no ETag. A repeated Idempotency-Key returns 409 idempotency_outcome_unknown without creating another endpoint while the reservation is retained. After a lost response, discover the endpoint and deliberately rotate its secret; do not blindly recreate it. Redis expiry/eviction provides no durable exactly-once guarantee. Requires workspace-level API access management permission.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort duplicate suppression of this one-time response. The original successful response is returned to the caller but never retained in API log bodies or Redis replay results. Only an unresolved reservation is retained for 24 hours by default; a matching retry returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without repeating the operation or revealing its secret. A concurrent request returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use`; a changed request returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution. A 4xx rejection releases its reservation; interruption after execution or loss of the success response requires inspection and a deliberate new operation. Redis expiry/eviction or explicit server-side disabling removes protection; this is not durable exactly-once execution. Use the target GET to inspect current metadata and obtain its validator, then a new key only when intentionally rotating again.

parameters.description: Optional unique key for best-effort POST retry protection. Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

Redis reserves the key, the request runs with ordinary service transactions, then the successful response is cached separately for 24 hours by default. There is no request-wide transaction or atomic commit between the operation and its replay result. A matching cached response is replayed verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Redis loss/eviction or retention expiry can remove protection and allow re-execution. Uploads and chunked bodies are covered; multipart boundaries and JSON property order may differ. Retries still pass validation and current authorization; a later 403/404 does not undo the original operation. A changed payload returns 422 `idempotency_key_mismatch`. A recent active reservation returns 409 `idempotency_key_in_use` with `Retry-After`. A retry with an unresolved key, including an unfinished reservation older than 5 minutes, returns 409 `idempotency_outcome_unknown` without `Retry-After`. This timeout does not release the reservation or permit re-execution while it is retained. Inspect the affected resource before starting a new operation; do not blindly reuse an unresolved key after expiry. A 4xx rejection releases the reservation, allowing the same key to be retried after correcting the cause. A 5xx or interruption after execution starts leaves it unresolved. An unavailable reservation store returns 503 before execution; an oversized request returns 413. Cache-save failure or a response over the cache limit preserves the original success status, headers and body; only future retries become unresolved. When idempotency is explicitly disabled by server configuration, the header is ignored and requests execute normally without retry protection. Use a new unique key for each intended operation.

parameters.description: Optional precondition. Send the quoted ETag from a GET of this resource. The mutation only runs if a strong tag matches the current representation, checked under the write lock. A comma-separated list is allowed; '*' requires an existing representation. Weak tags never match. Omit this header for an unconditional write. For an action, use the ETag from GET of the target resource, without the action suffix. A stale tag returns 412; read the current state before retrying.

post.description: Replaces the endpoint signing secret and returns the new material only in this original response. Existing in-flight deliveries may already hold the old secret. Optional If-Match uses the ordinary endpoint GET validator. This one-time response is excluded from API log bodies and Redis replay results; it has Cache-Control: no-store and no ETag. A reused Idempotency-Key returns idempotency_outcome_unknown (409) without executing again while its reservation is retained. Redis expiry/eviction provides no durable exactly-once guarantee. If the response is lost, inspect the endpoint and deliberately rotate using a new key and current validator; GET never reveals signing material. Requires workspace-level API access management permission.

tags.description: Read the workspace your API key belongs to. A workspace holds your stacks, projects and members.
tags.name: Workspaces

tags.description: List, update and remove the members of the workspace.
tags.name: Members

tags.description: Invite people to the workspace by email, and manage pending invitations and the stacks they will join.
tags.name: Invitations

tags.description: Read the roles a workspace member can have.
tags.name: Workspace Roles

tags.description: Check the API key a request is made with, and manage the workspace's API keys and their permissions.
tags.name: API Keys

tags.description: Read the file formats LingoHub supports, the upload limits and the export formats a project can use.
tags.name: Capabilities

tags.description: List every locale LingoHub supports, to find the language codes you can add to a project or stack.
tags.name: Locales

tags.description: Manage stacks. A stack holds the languages, members and texts its projects share: a `PUBLIC` stack can serve several projects, a `PRIVATE` stack belongs to one project.
tags.name: Stacks

tags.description: Manage who has explicit access to a stack, with which role and language permissions.
tags.name: Stack Members

tags.description: Read the permissions a member effectively has in a stack.
tags.name: Stack Member Permissions

tags.description: Read the roles a stack member can have.
tags.name: Stack Roles

tags.description: Manage the target languages configured for a stack. The stack's languages are shared by every project assigned to that stack.
tags.name: Stack Languages

tags.description: Manage the localization projects of the workspace. A project holds resource files, languages and texts.
tags.name: Projects

tags.description: Read and replace a project's import, export, format, key and placeholder settings.
tags.name: Project Settings

tags.description: Manage the target languages configured for a project. Project languages are scoped to a branch.
tags.name: Project Languages

tags.description: Move a project to another stack, or detach it into a stack of its own, as an async job.
tags.name: Project Moves

tags.description: Manage branches within a project. Branches isolate translation work; each project has exactly one default branch that cannot be deleted.
tags.name: Branches

tags.description: List and manage the resource files of a project branch, with their format, path and translation status per language.
tags.name: Resources

tags.description: List and manage the keys of a resource file. Each key is one entry of the file and points to the segment that holds its texts.
tags.name: Keys

tags.description: Read and update segments. A segment holds the texts that one or more keys share, so a change affects every key that uses it.
tags.name: Segments

tags.description: Read and update texts: one per segment and language, including the source, with its variants and workflow status.
tags.name: Texts

tags.description: Read the rows of a CSV resource.
tags.name: CSV Rows

tags.description: Manage the labels of the workspace. Labels tag segments, so you can categorize and filter content.
tags.name: Labels

tags.description: Upload screenshots that show translators and LINAs where a text appears. An image belongs to one project language and can be attached to segments of that project.
tags.name: Context Images

tags.description: Import resource files as async jobs, and see what each import changed.
tags.name: Imports

tags.description: Export translations as async jobs and download the result.
tags.name: Exports

tags.description: Manage glossaries within a workspace. Glossaries contain terms and their translations.
tags.name: Glossaries
